correctness.rationale: The decomposition into outer-negation parity and syntactic core is unique. For each core B, independent truth/falsity bits are permitted; the sole restriction is t_circle=1 implies (t_parent,f_parent)=(1,0) or (0,1). A simultaneous positive and negative requirement on the parent contradicts a positive circle requirement. Conversely absent that triple, choosing (1,1) only when both parent signs are demanded, (1,0) when positive alone, and (0,1) otherwise satisfies every circle requirement. The induction extending signed unary bits to all binary connectives enforces De Morgan, involution and the one-way circle implication, including nested circles and all infinite premises. Every proper subset of a prohibited triple is satisfiable, so the exact 3-Helly statement follows. An independent enumeration of 6,564 core-forest premise subsets for sizes <=4 matched the criterion; this is only a finite sanity check. Linear scanning assumes unshared input tree or linear-time syntax interning.
